lede: Tuesday is the one to watch: a newly sworn-in Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write state wildfire standards into Telluride's Land Use Code covering landscaping, trees, and historic review — if it passes, it's law. The Housing Authority meets the same day to work out a tricky primary-residency policy for dependents in split-custody households, and Thursday Planning and Zoning digs into three Town-owned development proposals in the Accommodations 2 zone, including the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code.
New primary-residency policy for split-custody dependents could affect housing eligibility.
Town-owned Carhenge redevelopment and two other projects up for land-use review.
